sampling_method: Every own-result cell in frame_locations was assigned a contiguous 1-based index in reading order, giving a population of 1..331. Location order is the page and in-page position of each location's first result-bearing content; a location carrying no result cell is ordered by the position of its heading instead. That distinction is load-bearing twice: Section 4.4 sits after Tables 4-6 on page 6 because its 8%/25% restatement is printed below them although its heading is on page 5, while Section 5.4 sits on page 7 with its heading because it carries no cell at all. Within a table the order is row-major -- rows top-to-bottom in printed order, and within each row left-to-right across that row's own-result numeric columns only, skipping citation-only rows entirely and skipping non-result columns wherever they fall. Excluded as non-result columns throughout: Table 3's #parameters, Table 12's #Texts, and the Pre-train #Images column of Tables 5-8; architecture-spec and corpus-size figures are hyperparameter or dataset_statistic, matching dino.json's exclusion of #params/dim/blocks/heads. A cell printed '-' or 'N.A.' is not a cell and is skipped (Table 2's None row prints no noise ratio; baseline rows of Tables 5, 7, 8 and 10 print '-' in places, but no BLIP row does anywhere in the paper). Ownership is assigned per row from the citation markers, which this paper prints consistently: every prior-work row of Tables 5, 7, 10 and 11 carries an inline '(Author et al., year)' and every BLIP row carries none; Tables 6, 8 and 9 print their baseline rows without an inline citation, but those rows name prior methods the paper compares against (CLIP, ALIGN, ALBEF; LXMERT, UNITER, VL-T5/BART, OSCAR, SOHO, VILLA, UNIMO, SimVLM; VD-BERT, VD-ViLBERT) and are cited in the surrounding text, so they are baselines too. The per-cell ownership rule that split convnext's rows does not fire anywhere here: no caption in this paper attributes any competitor's number to the authors, there is no throughput/FPS column measured for every row, and the paper contains no rerun or reimplementation of a prior model, so the entire own-result frame is the BLIP rows of Tables 5-11 plus the six ablation tables that contain no baseline row at all (Tables 1, 2, 3, 4, 12, 13). Retrieval rows contribute one cell per printed recall column -- twelve for a Table 5 row (COCO TR R@1/R@5/R@10, COCO IR R@1/R@5/R@10, Flickr30K TR R@1/R@5/R@10, Flickr30K IR R@1/R@5/R@10), six for a Table 6 row -- and captioning rows one cell per printed C/S/B@4 column, per this file's rule that one token holding two metrics is two cells. A delta stated in prose with no absolute printed beside it counts as its own cell: the abstract's +2.7%, +2.8% and +1.6%, Section 5.1's +2.7%, Section 5.3's +1.64% and Section 5.6's +12.4% are each counted, and each is a separate printed instance even where two of them restate one comparison at different precision (+1.6% in the abstract against +1.64% in Section 5.3). Comparative multipliers ('13x more training data', '13x more pre-training data') are excluded as ratios rather than reported values, matching dino.json's exclusion of '10x less parameters'. The six noise-ratio cells (Table 2's 19%/25%, Table 4's 8%/25%, Section 4.4's restatement of 8%/25%) are counted as own results -- they are measurements the paper's own filter produced and are used as evidence for the nucleus-sampling and decoupling arguments -- but the reading is genuinely arguable against dataset_statistic; none of the six was drawn, so the ambiguity does not reach any label. random.seed(20260810); random.sample(range(1, 332), 15) drew {1, 3, 25, 28, 49, 57, 139, 166, 182, 197, 214, 216, 244, 295, 305}; each label below records its draw as frame_index.
